svg.title: Inside a .mcpb bundle: the archive, and the signature appended after it
svg.desc: The bundle is drawn as one file read top to bottom. The upper region, outlined in terracotta and labelled ZIP content, lists what the archive holds: manifest.json, which is required and the only required file, a server directory holding whatever the entry point names, an optional icon at the root, and everything else the server needs. A heavy rule across the whole file is labelled the ZIP ends here, and everything below it is outside the archive: a block labelled the signature, if signed, holding a marker reading MCPB_SIG_V1, a four-byte little-endian length prefix, a DER-encoded PKCS number seven SignedData structure, and a closing MCPB_SIG_END marker. Notes below say the signature is detached, so the archive is never rewritten and unpacking a signed bundle behaves as it did before, and that verify reports a bundle as signed, self-signed or unsigned while what a host does with that at install time is undocumented. On the right, an upper panel lists the manifest's five required top-level fields, the three fields its server object requires on every server type, and the four permitted types, noting that dxt_version survives as an alias while the .dxt file extension does not. A lower panel outlined in amber tabulates five primary sources for the default manifest_version and the three different answers they give, and concludes that since validation accepts 0.1 through 0.4 the safe move is to write the field yourself. A closing line notes that the latest published release is v2.1.2 from December 2025, and that several documented commands exist only on the main branch.
svg.text: A ZIP file, and a signature that begins after it ends
manifest.json is the only required file. A signature is appended past the archive, never inside it.
required, and the only required file
Detached: the archive is never rewritten, so unpacking
a signed bundle works exactly as it did before.
verify reports signed, self-signed, or unsigned. What a host
does with that at install time is undocumented.
all three required, on every server type
dxt_version is still accepted as an alias. The .dxt extension is not.
Validation accepts 0.1 through 0.4, so the safe move is
to write the field yourself and never rely on a default.
The latest published release is v2.1.2, from 2025-12-04. clean, unpack and pack --manifest are real on main, and not on npm.
